title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
statement: `nums` is sorted in nondecreasing order. Remove the duplicates in place so each unique value appears once, preserving order. Return the compacted list of unique values.
hints: Because the array is sorted, a duplicate is always equal to the previous kept value.
A slow pointer marks the last unique value written.
Copy nums[fast] onto the next slot only when it differs from the last kept value.

approaches.name: Set then sort
approaches.explanation: Correct but ignores the sorted input.

approaches.name: Slow and fast pointers
approaches.explanation: One forward scan writes each new value once.

editorial: Initialize the write pointer at 1 if the array is non-empty. For each later value, write it and advance only when it differs from the value just written. The prefix of length equal to the write pointer is the answer.
